messages.author: 05dddafe48e2273c
messages.subject: point-level density/variance estimates
parts:
Hi all!

I have point count data from 2 breeding seasons, each point only visited
once. I am wanting point-level density estimates to use in a regression on
habitat variables. I first used model selection to compare effects of
covariates. Then I used the top model to estimate density. In the
estimates tab, I checked the boxes to estimate density and detection
function by global and sample (as a preiovus post reply indicated). This
method does not seem to produce the right results - several points with
detections have no variance around them. When I only use the global
detection function, the results are more reasonable and include variance.
However, no variance is calculated for those points with no detections.
Since there is a probability of not detecting a bird that is present,
shouldn't there be a predicted density estimate for every point. Do I need
to calculate variance using the bootstrap method?

Thanks for any help!

Jennifer Reidy
University of Missouri

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: point-level density/variance estimates
parts:
Jennifer, it sounds to me like you might be better modelling the counts
as described in section 4.5 of the 2004 advanced distance sampling
book. However, failing that, you will need to have a global detection
function model (your posting was unclear on this point), possibly using
the mcds engine if detectability may be a function of your habitat
covariates. Of course, for any point with no detections, estimated
density will be zero, and the variance estimate will also be zero.
Bootstrapping won't help with that, and in any case, the main method of
bootstrapping in Distance is to resamples sampling units (points here),
which doesn't help you. Generally for point data, there aren't
sufficient data to estimate density reliably by point, except by
developing a model for the counts, for example as in section 4.5 of the
2004 book.

Steve
